# Summary
### Chapter Key Takeaways

- References borrow data without transferring ownership.
- For the same ordinary borrowed place, shared and exclusive mutable access cannot conflict; interior-mutability types provide controlled alternatives.
- Dangling references are prohibited at compile time.
- Slice references (`&[T]` and `&str`) provide borrowed views of contiguous elements or UTF-8 bytes without allocating a new collection.
